result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Both answers rank the distorted-letters check and the form-wiping timeout as the top blockers, and both end with keyboard and screen-reader testing. B labels every finding with a severity (Blocker, Major, Minor), the evidence it saw and an effort estimate, and it places the long alt text clearly as a low-severity quick win. A shows priority only by order, puts labels, contrast, autocomplete and alt text together in one 'about 1 day' block, and leans on WCAG citations. B's 'Not checked' list adds a few generic items (200% zoom, forced colours) not drawn from the screens, so it loses a point on padding. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Both answers rank the CAPTCHA and the form-wiping timeout as the top blockers and give concrete fixes for labels and errors. A labels each finding with a severity, says where its evidence came from, and clearly marks the long alt text as a minor one-minute fix. B puts the alt fix in the same tier as labels and errors, and adds checklist items the screens don't support (paste in the password field, a real form element, required-field marking, red-border contrast), along with WCAG citations that are sometimes a stretch.
